messages:
Ravi Menon: Heads-up — BigBank wants to run a 10-day POC but will not send live data until we provide: signed DPA (incl. 2021 SCCs), completed SIG/CAIQ, and a DSAR deletion proof template. Need quick alignment on who owns each deliverable.
Clara Li: I can own the DPA exchange and SCCs. We should offer our standard clause: 'delete customer data and outputs derived from that data on request.' Call out embedding behaviour.
Noah Reed: I'll take CAIQ + evidence. Plan: network diagram, IAM screenshots, MFA proof, and a short runbook showing DSAR -> verify -> delete -> audit-hash. ETA 36-48h.
Jess Ortiz: Ops note: for hosted POC we can set persist_embeddings=false and disable long-term logs; default retention is 30d but we can reduce to 0 for POC on request. If they insist, Dedicated can route to customer-owned storage.
ComplianceBot: Automated: control-evidence export started (ticket SLS-709). Expected ready in ~40h.
Ravi Menon: Pricing/terms: propose capped free credits for 10 days and a one-page POC scope + success criteria. Also include explicit allowed-data list (no production PII).
Clara Li: Sending DPA+SCC PDF to their counsel today. If they redline 'derivatives' beyond reasonable bounds escalate to legal@redwood.
Noah Reed: Will draft the DSAR deletion proof template (includes sample API call, verification checklist, and an example audit-hash entry). Will paste CAIQ answers into thread when ready.
Jess Ortiz: Quick operational caveat: if debug mode enabled we may temporarily persist traces — include a checkbox in POC terms to opt-in and set TTL.
Ravi Menon: Great — owners: Clara = DPA/SCC, Noah = CAIQ + DSAR template, Jess = ops config notes, Ill draft POC scope + outreach. Target: CAIQ + runbook in 48h, DPA sent today. Any blockers?
Clara Li: None. I'll cc legal on the email and request countersign timeline from their counsel.
Noah Reed: No blockers. I'll include the audit-hash example and a short paragraph explaining tamper-evidence.
Ravi Menon: Thanks team — I'll update BigBank and ask them to upload their SIG file here.
